Security.0103.description: Certificate management packages or configurations detected. This may indicate the application is using local or custom certificate handling, which could require adjustments when migrating to Azure. Consider using Azure Key Vault Certificates for secure storage, lifecycle management, and integration with Azure services.
Security.0103.title: Certificate management dependency detected

Scale.0001.description:
Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Scale.0001.title: Static content detected

Database.0002.description:
SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
    1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
    2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
    3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Database.0002.title: SQL database connection detected

links.title: Migrate SQL Server database to Azure

Database.0003.description:
System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.
Database.0003.title: System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected

Security.0003.description:
Hardcoded sensitive data detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, externalize secrets to Key Vault/App Configuration; use managed identity instead of passwords or embedded connection strings.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Avoid placing sensitive data such as passwords, ids, tokens etc., directly in config files and code since it compromises the security of your application.

Use Azure App Configuration or Azure KeyVault to store secrets.
Security.0003.title: Hardcoded sensitive data detected

Local.0006.description:
Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local.0006.title: Hardcoded URLs detected

security.title: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
security.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

evidence.explanation: CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue and CatalogDBInitializer.GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence read Int64 database sequence values and cast them directly to int. Values outside the Int32 range are truncated, potentially reusing or corrupting catalog identifiers.

security.title: Incorrect Calculation
security.description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

evidence.explanation: Default.Page_Load accepts route-provided size and index and passes them through without range checks. CatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated multiplies them as 32-bit integers for Skip and uses size in Take; the view model divides by pageSize. Extreme values can overflow the offset, and a zero size causes division by zero.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: ImageAzureStorage.UpLoadImageFromFile opens a FileStream with File.OpenRead and uploads it, but never disposes or closes the stream after the upload, leaving the resource unreleased.

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: ImageAzureStorage.UpLoadImageFromFile opens a file handle using File.OpenRead and does not close or dispose it after UploadFromStream completes.

security.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
security.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

evidence.explanation: The route-controlled size is passed directly to CatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated, where it is used as the Take count and the results are materialized with ToList without a maximum bound. A very large page size can cause an unnecessarily large result set and memory consumption.

security.title: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

evidence.explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. CatalogServiceMock stores catalogItems in a mutable List and CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem modify it without a lock, allowing concurrent requests to race.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. CatalogServiceMock stores catalogItems in a mutable List and CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem modify it without a lock, allowing concurrent requests to race.

security.title: Improper Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. CatalogServiceMock stores catalogItems in a mutable List and CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem modify it without a lock, allowing concurrent requests to race.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. CatalogServiceMock stores catalogItems in a mutable List and CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem modify it without a lock, allowing concurrent requests to race.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: PicUploader.UploadImage logs only a generic processing-start message. The invalid-image rejection path returns HTTP 400 without recording the event, and successful uploads do not log the outcome or affected catalog item, leaving these security-relevant upload events without an auditable record.

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.

evidence.explanation: PicUploader.UploadImage reads itemId from the request form and passes the parsed value with the uploaded file to IImageService.UploadTempImage. ImageAzureStorage.UploadTempImage uses that externally supplied item ID and file.FileName to construct the Azure blob identifier (path + file.FileName.ToLower()) and uploads to that blob without restricting the selected catalog-item namespace. A caller can therefore select another item's blob namespace through the resource identifier.
